hypotheses.reasoning: The trigger was brief: template-svc-3 failed its liveness probe and restarted at 23:02:24 (#96), and full capacity was back by 23:02:59 (#99). After that, notification-svc's TemplateClient retried every 503 immediately with backoff turned off (#101, #106, #111). Each failed request became up to 4 calls, so inbound traffic to template-svc went to 3.2x and then 4.1x baseline (#110, #118). template-svc shed the extra load with 503s when its queue filled (#105, #121), which caused more retries. The loop keeps itself going, which is why the gateway 503s keep coming after capacity came back (#102, #115, #125, #137).
Retries with backoff turned off look like a misconfiguration. That setting is what turns a short blip into an outage that keeps going. I found no log showing when or how the setting was changed.
Probably unrelated: a single notif-worker message failed schema validation and went to the DLQ (#17). It's an isolated event with no link to the /v1/notify path.

verdict.recommendedAction: Stop the retry storm. Turn on exponential backoff with jitter, plus a retry budget or circuit breaker, in notification-svc's TemplateClient, or set retries to 1 for now. While the load drains, scale template-svc out or rate-limit /v1/notify at the gateway for a while. Then find out why backoff was off and why template-svc-3 failed its liveness probe.
